title: Machine-learning triage identifies a dormant wandering black hole in a galaxy’s outskirts
summary: The off-nuclear transient TDE 2025abcr revealed a dormant supermassive black hole about 9.3 kiloparsecs from its host galaxy’s center, with a mass described as similar to the Milky Way’s central black hole. A machine-learning program searching for tidal-disruption flares anywhere in the sky selected the event for follow-up three months after deployment; astronomers then collected multi-instrument evidence and interpreted it as the strongest known wandering-black-hole case. Its precise origin remains uncertain, with stripped remnant and black-hole-ejection scenarios both discussed.
organization: University of Maryland; NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; University of California Observatories and collaborators

evidence.tested: The off-nuclear transient TDE 2025abcr revealed a dormant supermassive black hole about 9.3 kiloparsecs from its host galaxy’s center, with a mass described as similar to the Milky Way’s central black hole.
evidence.unknown: The specific off-nuclear transient was AI-selected, but the paper’s evidence and interpretation are observational follow-up, not a model-generated discovery. The black hole’s formation history is unresolved; the host has no obvious surrounding galaxy at the black-hole position.
evidence.ai_role: Ranked the transient as a candidate tidal-disruption event away from a galaxy nucleus, prompting spectroscopic and multi-wavelength follow-up; the astrophysical interpretation relied on subsequent human analysis and observations.
